related_questions.question: What is an antibody test for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: COVID-19 antibody testing is a blood test. The test can provide information about how your body reacted to infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). SARS-CoV-2 is the name of the virus that causes coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19).

related_questions.snippet: An antibody serology test can check if your immune system should be able to protect you against certain diseases better. related_questions.question: How long do COVID antibodies stay in your system?
related_questions.snippet: The number and type of antibodies varied between people. But the levels usually remained stable over time. They slightly decreased six to eight months after infection. Immune cell levels also remained high.
related_questions.title: How Long Does Protection Last After COVID-19? - NIH News in Health

related_questions.question: What does a positive antibody test result indicate?
related_questions.snippet: A positive antibody test means the test has detected high levels of antibodies (above a certain amount) in your blood. It does NOT mean you are currently infected with COVID-19. The nucleocapsid antibody test detects antibodies that are produced by the immune system in response to COVID-19.

list.snippet: To determine if a person has been infected with COVID-19 in the past, even if they did not have symptoms.
To assess the level of immunity to COVID-19 after vaccination or natural infection.
IgG antibody test: Detects antibodies that provide long-term protection against reinfection.
IgM antibody test: Detects antibodies that indicate a recent infection within the past few weeks.
A blood sample is taken and analyzed in a laboratory.

list.title: Positive:
list.snippet: Indicates that the person has been infected with COVID-19 in the past and has developed antibodies.

list.title: Negative:
list.snippet: Indicates that the person has not been infected with COVID-19 or does not have detectable antibodies at the time of testing.
Antibody tests may not detect antibodies in people who have recently been infected or have a very low level of antibodies.
A positive result does not necessarily mean that a person is currently immune to COVID-19.
Discuss the results with a healthcare provider to understand their implications.
Vaccination or additional measures may be recommended based on the test results.

text_blocks.snippet: Note: It is important to consult with a healthcare professional for personalized medical advice and interpretation of test results.
